usage: wsp start <link> [--project <name>] [--agent <id>]
       [--model, --effort, --access <word>]
  a thread off a GitHub issue or pull request link, the issue or the pull
  request its first message; an issue's thread runs in the project folder, a
  pull request's in a worktree on its branch

  --project    the project by name or id where two computers hold the link's
               repository; this computer's without it
  --agent      which agent runs the thread, by its catalog id (claude, codex,
               opencode, cursor); the project's own default without it
  --model      the model the turn runs on, by the agent's own slug
               (claude-sonnet-5); the thread's own without it
  --effort     how hard the agent thinks, by its own word (low, medium, high,
               xhigh, max); absent on a new thread means the agent's default; on
               send, the thread's own
  --access     how far the agent may go without asking: ask, auto-edit, full or
               plan, refused where the agent has no such mode; without it, the
               project's, else the agent's default, else full
  --json       print the raw protocol values, one JSON object per line, with
               everything else on stderr
  --state      the state file the host serves
  --host       run the line against a host on your account, by the name wsp
               hosts lists it under; WSP_HOST names one for a whole shell

usage: wsp review <link|thread> [--agent <id>] [--model, --effort <word>]
  a reviewer thread on a pull request, read-only, whose review waits in wsp
  until you post it

  --agent     the reviewing agent, codex or claude, each at its read-only
              access; codex without it
  --model     the model the turn runs on, by the agent's own slug
              (claude-sonnet-5); the thread's own without it
  --effort    how hard the agent thinks, by its own word (low, medium, high,
              xhigh, max); absent on a new thread means the agent's default; on
              send, the thread's own
  --json      print the raw protocol values, one JSON object per line, with
              everything else on stderr
  --state     the state file the host serves
  --host      run the line against a host on your account, by the name wsp hosts
              lists it under; WSP_HOST names one for a whole shell

usage: wsp review post <thread> [--verdict comment|approve|request-changes]
       [--summary "<text>"]
  posts a reviewer thread's review on its pull request as you, its ticked
  comments on their lines

  --verdict    comment, approve or request-changes; the draft's own, the
               reviewer's word unless you changed it, without it
  --summary    the review's summary, written over the draft's
  --json       print the raw protocol values, one JSON object per line, with
               everything else on stderr
  --state      the state file the host serves
  --host       run the line against a host on your account, by the name wsp
               hosts lists it under; WSP_HOST names one for a whole shell

usage: wsp update <thread>
  merges the latest commits of the base into the branch of the folder the thread
  works in, or names the files that conflict

  --json     print the raw protocol values, one JSON object per line, with
             everything else on stderr
  --state    the state file the host serves
  --host     run the line against a host on your account, by the name wsp hosts
             lists it under; WSP_HOST names one for a whole shell

usage: wsp resize <thread> --size <cpu>x<memGb>
  moves the machine a thread runs on to another size its provider sells: a stop,
  then a resume at that size

  --size     the machine size as <cpu>x<memGb>, like 2x4; a size the provider
             does not offer is refused naming the ones it does
  --json     print the raw protocol values, one JSON object per line, with
             everything else on stderr
  --state    the state file the host serves
  --host     run the line against a host on your account, by the name wsp hosts
             lists it under; WSP_HOST names one for a whole shell

usage: wsp image
  the image this host owns: its version, its hash, whether it holds your
  sign-ins (an image built on Boat holds none), and the copy each place has
  built of it

  --json     print the raw protocol values, one JSON object per line, with
             everything else on stderr
  --state    the state file the host serves
  --host     run the line against a host on your account, by the name wsp hosts
             lists it under; WSP_HOST names one for a whole shell

usage: wsp image build <place> [--force]
  builds this host's image at a place from the record, its sign-ins coming from
  the vault and no sign-in run again

  --force    build again even where the place already holds this version
  --json     print the raw protocol values, one JSON object per line, with
             everything else on stderr
  --state    the state file the host serves
  --host     run the line against a host on your account, by the name wsp hosts
             lists it under; WSP_HOST names one for a whole shell

usage: wsp delete <thread> [--processes stop|keep] [--yes]
  takes a thread away, its turns and checkpoints with it, and the worktree wsp
  made for it once no other thread is in it, never the project folder, refused
  while one still runs processes, on this computer or a box, unless --processes
  says to stop or keep them

  --yes          go ahead without being asked
  --processes    stop ends every process the thread still runs beside its agent,
                 by identity, before it goes; keep leaves them running; refused
                 without it while any run
  --json         print the raw protocol values, one JSON object per line, with
                 everything else on stderr
  --state        the state file the host serves
  --host         run the line against a host on your account, by the name wsp
                 hosts lists it under; WSP_HOST names one for a whole shell

usage: wsp forget <workspace> [--yes]

  machine exists

  --yes      go ahead without being asked
  --json     print the raw protocol values, one JSON object per line, with
             everything else on stderr
  --state    the state file the host serves
  --host     run the line against a host on your account, by the name wsp hosts
